doc.title: Rob Mounsey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 9, 2025

title: Giving every orchestra player a real part; pops orchestra arrangements
summary: On the bassoon question he talks about writing idiomatic parts for orchestra players, his pops work, and the poor arrangements pops orchestras get.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Have you ever been in a situation where you look at your score and you say, “You know they hired two bassoon players and I hardly have anything for them. I should give them something to play?

Interesting you should choose the bassoon. I love the bassoon. I mean I love the bassoon in the orchestra, it’s a wonderful instrument. I do a lot of orchestral pops arrangements for Cincinnati Pops, Boston Pops and other orchestras and for events where they accompany singers. And I love the orchestra madly, but I think it’s very important when creating those things to give every single person a reason to be there. You know? And to put in front of that second bassoonist a part that that musician recognizes as a bassoon part. You know? This is a part for me, it makes me sound good, it makes me feel good, it lays nicely on the instrument, you know, displays an understanding of the registers of the instrument, and now I know why I missed all those baseball games as a kid because I had lessons and I was practicing. You know I had the highest highest respect for those orchestra musicians, especially the string players who were all my heroes. If you can play a violin or cello or viola and make it sound beautiful, I take my hat off to you. Because those instruments are so insanely hard to play. And they deserve to have parts that make sense for them and make them sound good and make them remember why they do this, because they love it and because they sound beautiful doing it. The pops orchestras, I’m getting away from your question a little bit because this is not so much about recording as about live performance but those pops orchestras have to confront a lot of really terrible arrangements.
